title: Stalk criterion for scalar restriction on an open site
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X$, $\varphi:R\to\mathcal O_X$ a ring-sheaf map, $U\subset X$ open and $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose for each $x\in U$ the module $G_x$, restricted along $\varphi_x:R_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], is flat over $R_x$. Then the restriction of $G$ to the localized site over $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], with scalars restricted by $\varphi|_U$, is flat as an $R|_U$-module [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Neither quasi-coherence nor a nonempty open is required.

proof.text: Regard R as the structure sheaf of a ringed space Y with the same carrier as X, and restrict G scalars along φ to obtain H. Its additive presheaf is exactly the additive presheaf of G. Represent a scalar and a module element by germs, restrict both to the intersection of their neighborhoods, and use germ_smul for both rings and stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply for φ. This proves the identity on additive stalks is R_x-linear, and transports the assumed flatness to H_x.

For an exact short complex C of modules on the localized site over U, apply exact extension by zero E to get an exact ambient complex. Tensor E(C) with H. In U, stalkTensorIso and the assumed flatness give exactness; outside U the middle stalk of E(C) is zero, and its tensor is zero, so the stalk complex is exact. Stalk detection gives exactness of the ambient tensor complex.

Apply exact open restriction V to the ambient tensor complex. The natural tensor-restriction comparison identifies this with tensoring V(E(C)) by V(H). The extension/restriction unit is invertible, naturally identifying C with V(E(C)), so C tensor V(H) is exact. The additive tensor functor thus preserves homology, hence finite limits and finite colimits, which is IsFlat. Scalar restriction commutes with overFunctor sectionwise, so this is the stated module. No points outside U require flatness of H; for empty U the same extension-by-zero proof applies.

lean.statement:
theorem isFlat_open_scalarRestriction_of_stalks
    (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (R : X.carrier.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u})
    (φ : R ⟶ X.sheaf) (U : Opens X) (G : Modules X)
    (hflat : ∀ (x : X), x ∈ U →
      Module.Flat ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} x).obj R.obj)
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat.{u} x).map φ.hom).hom).obj
        ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).obj G))) :
    let α := ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).overPullback CommRingCat.{u} U).map φ
    let B := (sheafCompose ((Opens.grothendieckTopology X).over U)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map α
    SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars B).obj
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X) U).obj G))
